subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should the Slack plugin add Slack RTS as a separate assistant action-token search path, and what token containment and scope rules should govern it relative to user-token `search.messages`?
rationale: The requested capability is valid but security-sensitive: it handles event-scoped Slack action tokens and workspace search results, and existing adjacent work uses a different Slack search API.

options.title: Approve a narrow RTS contract
options.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, read-only action exposure, docs, focused tests, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Consolidate Slack search first
options.body: Define one Slack search contract that covers both RTS and user-token `search.messages`, then update or replace the adjacent search work to match it.

options.title: Defer workspace search
options.body: Keep Slack workspace search out until maintainers are ready to own the token, privacy, scope, and live-validation burden.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow RTS contract
recommendation.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, read-only action exposure, docs, focused tests, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal for Slack assistant-thread context is Peter Steinberger's 6b525023d4 work, and this issue needs a Slack assistant/product-boundary decision.
